items.desc: New trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US could begin in October, according to Kyiv and Moscow. Few expect a breakthrough, but Ukraine is seeking a partial de-escalation to help it get through the winter.

items.title: Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
items.titleOrig: Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
items.desc: Donald Trump, under fire for record US diesel prices, claims Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking energy targets. Russia said nothing; Ukraine said "we expect specifics from our partners" on any such move.

items.title: Donald Trump dismisses concerns about dangers of AI
items.titleOrig: Donald Trump dismisses concerns about dangers of AI
items.desc: The president called efforts to slow the development of artificial intelligence a "sick conspiracy," claiming they only serve China. Market leaders have warned of the dangers of the pace of the technology's development.

items.title: Yemen's Houthis attack Saudis, seize crucial Red Sea islands
items.titleOrig: Yemen's Houthis attack Saudis, seize crucial Red Sea islands
items.desc: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have tightened their grip on a key shipping route, capturing two strategic Red Sea islands. The closure of another global transport route is the latest ripple effect of the US war with Iran.

items.title: Women's Basketball World Cup: Can Germany harness a boom?
items.titleOrig: Women's Basketball World Cup: Can Germany harness a boom?
items.desc: Germany thrilled fans at the Women's Basketball World Cup. But even if this sparked a boom in the women's game, the infrastructure simply isn't ready for it.

items.title: IPO 'for the people' is out of reach for many in Nigeria
items.titleOrig: IPO 'for the people' is out of reach for many in Nigeria
items.desc: Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?

items.title: Germany news: Merz urges CDU discipline as pressure grows
items.titleOrig: Germany news: Merz urges CDU discipline as pressure grows
items.desc: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has urged his party to stay disciplined as pressure grows over his leadership. Meanwhile, Germany's homeownership rate has fallen to its lowest level in 20 years. DW has the latest.

items.title: Ukraine: AfD questions German aid, Berlin remains committed
items.titleOrig: Ukraine: AfD questions German aid, Berlin remains committed
items.desc: Emboldened by its win in Saxony-Anhalt, the far-right Alternative for Germany wants the government to change its Ukraine and Russia policies. Berlin is staying the course, but support is fading — especially in the east.

items.title: The Crusades: How a medieval Holy War still shapes politics
items.titleOrig: The Crusades: How a medieval Holy War still shapes politics
items.desc: In 1095, the Catholic Church launched the Crusades: wars that left millions dead and whose legacy still shapes political and ideological conflicts.

items.title: Nepal: thousands still missing as flood recovery begins
items.titleOrig: Nepal: thousands still missing as flood recovery begins
items.desc: The Himalayan nation is moving from rescue operations to recovery, facing a $4.8 billion reconstruction bill amid renewed calls for climate justice.

items.title: EU leaders urge unity after Russian strike on train
items.titleOrig: EU leaders urge unity after Russian strike on train
items.desc: Russia's drone attack on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border has triggered EU calls to up support for Kyiv. Allies of Ukraine should show they "are not scared," said the bloc's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas.

items.title: Berlin businesswoman charged with spying for Russia
items.titleOrig: Berlin businesswoman charged with spying for Russia
items.desc: Prosecutors say the Berlin marketing executive used her political and military contacts to help a Russian intelligence officer gain access to influential circles and seek information on German defense policy.

items.title: India women's team refuse Asia Cup cricket trophy from Pakistan minister
items.titleOrig: India women's team refuse Asia Cup cricket trophy from Pakistan minister
items.desc: After beating Sri Lanka to win a record eighth Asia Cup title, the Indian women's cricket team skipped the trophy presentation with Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.

items.title: Pay to ghost your boss: Japan's resignation business
items.titleOrig: Pay to ghost your boss: Japan's resignation business
items.desc: Resignation agencies in Japan help employees leave their jobs seamlessly in just 15 minutes. Young people are especially eager to use their services.

items.title: Israeli minister accuses 'NAZA' filmmakers of 'treason'
items.titleOrig: Israeli minister accuses 'NAZA' filmmakers of 'treason'
items.desc: Israel's culture minister wants to strip the makers of a documentary on Israel's Gaza offensive of their citizenship. He accused the two of seeking "applause from antisemites around the world."

items.title: Finland: EU leaders meet to forge new Arctic policy
items.titleOrig: Finland: EU leaders meet to forge new Arctic policy
items.desc: European leaders are meeting over shipping, resources and security in the region amid pressure from the US, China and Russia. The EU sees the Arctic as key to its future security as melting ice makes it more accessible.

items.title: North Korea says recent drill shows 'huge destructive power'
items.titleOrig: North Korea says recent drill shows 'huge destructive power'
items.desc: North Korea carried out a coordinated live-fire exercise involving multiple weapons systems over the weekend. The drill came after the US, South Korea and Japan wrapped up five days of joint maritime exercises.

items.title: Can Iran replace sea trade with land routes?
items.titleOrig: Can Iran replace sea trade with land routes?
items.desc: Iran is shifting trade toward northern ports and land routes as its southern shipping faces a US blockade. Analysts say the corridors can keep essential goods moving, but cannot replace maritime trade.

items.title: In cosmopolitan Berlin, elections still closed to foreigners
items.titleOrig: In cosmopolitan Berlin, elections still closed to foreigners
items.desc: A quarter of Berlin residents will have no say in the German capital's city-state election because they lack citizenship. That's the highest proportion of residents excluded from the election yet, and many are unhappy.
